clue.text: American male in Prohibition who'd take people for a ride?

definitions.text: who'd take people for a ride?

indicators.note: in signals that the American male pieces sit inside the word for prohibition

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A Prohibition-era American gangster who'd take rivals for a ride, in the sinister sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take people for a ride' suggests gangland murder in the Prohibition setting, but here it is literal: a bus driver carries passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus driver literally takes passengers on journeys, a playful reading of the idiom for deceiving someone.

clue.text: Excel, having way, it's said, to produce vegetable

indicators.note: it's said signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to excel is to beat, and a way is a route; together they are spoken

explanation.surface: Someone excels at finding a way to grow vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAT (excel) plus ROUTE (way), when spoken, gives the root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The red root eaten in salads and borscht is a common garden vegetable.

clue.text: Old PM's turned up with the rest

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Robert Peel was a nineteenth-century British Prime Minister; with the 's he gives PEELS

explanation.surface: A former prime minister arrives along with the rest of his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is the body's nightly rest, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Excitement that can get Laura so upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the two named words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Something exciting enough to make Laura so upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred up or roused is a state of excitement, sexual or otherwise.

clue.text: Fliers in place executing one aerial attack

indicators.note: in places the fliers inside what is left of the place word
executing means killing off, so the letter for one is removed from the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place
I is the Roman numeral one
the RAF, Royal Air Force, are fliers

explanation.surface: Airmen in position, carrying out a single attack from the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executing' looks like carrying out the attack but signals the removal of I from SITE, leaving STE, which then holds RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Celebrate with something yellow in the spring?

definitions.meaning: to celebrate loudly or proclaim is to blow one's horn about it
the ...-shaped centre of a daffodil, a yellow spring flower

explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet is to proclaim proudly, and a daffodil's central cup is called its trumpet.

clue.text: Confusing 'anti-trade' Bill that could get treasonable Lords expelled

definitions.text: Bill that could get treasonable Lords expelled

indicators.note: confusing means the letters of the quoted phrase are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled bill against trade that could see treacherous peers thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: A bill of attainder was a historic Act of Parliament declaring someone guilty of treason without trial, stripping their titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainder was the legal forfeiture of rights and titles imposed by parliamentary bill on those convicted of treason.

clue.text: The woman turns up having to protect paintings etc. in underground shelters

indicators.note: to protect means the woman's word wraps around the paintings word
in a down entry turns up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: she refers to the woman
art covers paintings and similar works

explanation.surface: A woman goes underground to keep her art collection safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the woman's word to give EHS, and 'to protect' makes it wrap the paintings word; 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Earths are the burrows of foxes and badgers, their shelters beneath the ground.

clue.text: See large beast scratch finally with two insects around

indicators.note: around means the first insect goes about the final letter of scratch

parts.note: a bee is one insect

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word scratch

parts.note: a moth is the second insect

explanation.surface: Come and see a huge animal scratching, with a couple of bugs buzzing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting you to look, not the definition; 'around' has the first insect wrap the last letter of 'scratch', and 'with' joins on the second insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is the biblical giant beast, now any enormous creature or thing.

clue.text: Hero devours unusual dish to begin with

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of the two words are put in an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A hero greedily eats a strange dish as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the French term for a starter, borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names small appetisers served before the main meal, a dish to start with.

clue.text: Says crazy people should be beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the word for crazy people is cut off

parts.note: nutters is British slang for crazy people

explanation.surface: Someone declares that lunatics ought to be executed.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak words aloud is to say them, so voicing and saying are synonyms.

clue.text: Support for President initially

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word President

explanation.surface: Backing for the President right from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds up or supports, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Illumination in only half of street — one difficult situation

indicators.note: only half of takes the first three of the six letters of street

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Only half the street has lights, which makes for a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A long fluorescent tube light is a form of illumination, often fitted in kitchens and offices.

clue.text: Endless comfort I had embracing sweetheart, being made secure

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for comfort is dropped

parts.note: to console is to comfort

indicators.note: embracing means the contraction for I had wraps round the sweetheart word

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
a date is a sweetheart, someone you go out with

explanation.surface: Endless comfort from a lover's embrace makes one feel secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consolidated has been strengthened and made firm, so it is being made secure.

clue.text: Sitting outside church in withdrawn group

indicators.note: outside means the sitting word goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: a session is a sitting, as of a court or parliament
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A meeting held outside church by a group that has withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A secession can be a breakaway body, as in the Vienna Secession of artists who withdrew from the academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A secession is a breakaway, and the term also names the group of seceders themselves.

clue.text: Conservative worker involved in exploit is moved to another area

indicators.note: involved in means the two pieces are placed within the exploit word

parts.note: a deed is an exploit or feat
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A Conservative worker caught up in some scheme is relocated.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents are said to be decanted when moved out to other housing, as liquid is poured into another vessel.

clue.text: A thousand blokes in bed with stars, according to reports!

indicators.note: in places the thousand and blokes inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
men are blokes
Aries is a sign of the zodiac, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that many men are in bed with celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like celebrities in the gossip-column picture, but it is the constellation Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: Commentaries are spoken or written accounts of events, that is reports.

clue.text: Took advantage of sunny weather?

parts.note: plays on the proverb about making the most of an opportunity while the sun shines, literally drying cut grass on a sunny day

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exploited an opportunity, from farmers drying grass while the sun shines.

clue.text: Eject number of people coming to meeting?

definitions.meaning: to eject is to throw someone out

definitions.text: number of people coming to meeting?
definitions.meaning: the attendance figure at an event or election

explanation.definitionFit: To throw out is to expel, and the noun form means the attendance recorded at an event.

clue.text: Bit of a hand that's chewed?

definitions.text: Bit of a hand that's chewed?

parts.words: Bit of a hand that's chewed?
parts.note: a hand is also a bunch of a certain yellow fruit, each piece being eaten

explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of these fruits is called a hand, and each one in it is a finger to be eaten.

clue.text: Loony eavesdrops — gets ignored

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lunatic who eavesdrops is not taken any notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overlooked or skipped means being ignored, as when someone is not chosen for promotion.

clue.text: Fraudulent scheme of rascal cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the rascal word is removed

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal

explanation.surface: A con trick worked by a rogue is stopped early.
explanation.definitionFit: A con or swindle is a dishonest scheme to cheat people of money.

clue.text: Review creates problem at university

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone at university finds a review causes a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise the main points at the end is to review them briefly.

clue.text: Area within county capital given hospital

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A county town with a hospital has been built in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'county capital' reads as one phrase, but 'county' belongs to the definition and the capital is Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a small administrative or church district within a county.

clue.text: Great crime creates ill-will — men must be caught

indicators.note: must be caught means the men abbreviation is held inside the ill-will word

parts.note: enmity is hostility or ill-will
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A terrible crime causes hatred, and the perpetrators must be arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword shorthand for soldiers or men.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity in its traditional sense is a grave crime or monstrous wickedness.

clue.text: Ruffles making a nasty sound, audibly

indicators.note: audibly signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken, not spelled

parts.note: a noise is a nasty or unwelcome sound

explanation.surface: Something ruffled makes an unpleasant noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle someone's feathers is to irritate them, so ruffles and irritates are synonyms.

clue.text: Silly little woman stands the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: Di is a short form of the name Diana
to put something is to stand it somewhere

explanation.surface: A foolish young woman stands facing the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: DI plus PUTS read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and silly are synonyms, both meaning foolish or lacking sense.
